topIssues.title: op-proposer: HasProposedSince reverts on SuperPermissionedDisputeGame (type 5)
topIssues.author: pauldowman
topIssues.body:
op-proposer's dedup scan reads `claimData(0)` on every recent game (`op-proposer/contracts/disputegamefactory.go:139`, via `HasProposedSince` → `gameAtIndex`, using the hardcoded `FaultDisputeGameABI`). `SuperPermissionedDisputeGame` (game type 5) has no `claimData` — it exposes `rootClaim` / `gameCreator` / `proposer` instead — so the call reverts once any type-5 game is within the lookback window. Since `HasProposedSince` runs every proposal cycle (`driver.go:166`) and scans all recent games regardless of type, this breaks proposing against a factory that has type-5 games.

Submitting a type-5 game itself works: the `create(gameType, root, extraData)` path is game-type-agnostic and the `SuperRootProof` extraData op-proposer already builds (for type 9) is byte-for-byte what `SuperPermissionedDisputeGame.initialize()` decodes and hashes. Only the read-back breaks.

### Fix
- Make `gameAtIndex` type-aware: for type 5, read `rootClaim()` + `gameCreator()`/`proposer()` instead of `claimData(0)`.

### Test coverage gaps
This went unnoticed because the `super-at-genesis` and `super-via-upgrade` acceptance tests wire a type-5 proposer (`attachSuperChallengerAndProposer`, `multichain_super_at_genesis.go:24`) but only assert deployment shape (respected game type, impl present/absent) — they never verify the proposer creates or resolves a game.
- Add acceptance coverage that a type-5 proposer actually proposes and the game resolves `DEFENDER_WINS`.
- Extend the cross-ABI compatibility test (`op-proposer/contracts/disputegamefactory_test.go:29-30`, currently only `FaultDisputeGame` + `SuperFaultDisputeGame`) to include `SuperPermissionedDisputeGame`.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Failing test reproduces the `claimData` revert on the `SuperPermissionedDisputeGame` ABI, then passes after the fix.
- [ ] A proposer watching a factory containing type-5 games no longer errors during its dedup scan, regardless of its own configured game type.
- [ ] Cross-ABI test covers `SuperPermissionedDisputeGame`.
- [ ] Acceptance test verifies a type-5 game is proposed and resolves.

### Note (operational)
The contract enforces `tx.origin == proposer()`, so op-proposer's txmgr EOA must be the designated `proposer()` — no relayer in between. Worth documenting.

topIssues.title: kona-sp1: Implement super aggregation program
topIssues.author: Inphi
topIssues.body:
### Goal

Add an SP1 `super-aggregation` program that recursively verifies `super-range` and consolidation proofs, then emits the public values expected by `ZKDisputeGame.prove`.

### Inputs

- `l1Head`
- `startingRootHash`
- `rootClaim`
- `l2SequenceNumber`
- `prover`
- range proof public values + proofs
- consolidation proof public values + proofs
- Interim vkey for range/consolidation programs (Depends on https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21412. This can be omitted for the time being until we're ready for integration testing with the `ZKDisputeGame`.)

### Behavior

The aggregation program should recursively verify all child proofs and enforce:

- full timestamp coverage through `l2SequenceNumber`
- full chain coverage for each timestamp
- range outputs match corresponding consolidation outputs
- previous-super-root chaining across ranges
- final computed super root equals `rootClaim`
- every child range proof is bound to the same `l1Head` as the dispute game
- prover address is bound into the final public values

### Final Public Values

Commit exactly the ABI encoding used by `ZKDisputeGame.prove`:

```solidity
abi.encode(
    l1Head,
    startingRootHash,
    rootClaim,
    l2SequenceNumber,
    prover
)
```

### Interim Vkey Mode

For initial development, aggregation may accept range/consolidation vkey as private or host-supplied inputs.
This is **not production-sound** until range program vkey is embedded in the aggregation program or publicly bound by the verifier path.

### Tests

Add coverage for:

- final public-values ABI encoding
- dynamic-vkey input serialization
- valid range/consolidation aggregation
- timestamp coverage gaps
- chain coverage gaps
- broken range/consolidation matching
- broken previous-super-root chaining
- L1 ancestry mismatch
- final root-claim mismatch
- prover binding

topIssues.title: op-proposer: select proposal sources by root format instead of interop mode
topIssues.author: pauldowman
topIssues.body:
op-proposer classifies proposal sources using stale `preInteropGameTypes` and `postInteropGameTypes` lists. The output-root list omits `CANNON_KONA` type 8, while the super-root list still contains retired `SUPER_CANNON` type 4 and omits its replacement, `SUPER_CANNON_KONA` type 9. The current implementation also selects the proposal adapter from the RPC flag: `--rollup-rpc` always selects the output-root adapter, while `--supernode-rpcs` selects the `superroot_atTimestamp` adapter.

  A SafeDB-enabled op-node now serves `superroot_atTimestamp`, so standalone type-5 and type-9 proposers should be able to use their existing `--rollup-rpc` endpoint without moving that URL to the misleading `--supernode-rpcs` flag. Replace the pre-/post-interop classification with output-root/super-root classification, use the output-root adapter for type 8, and use the super-root adapter for types 5 and 9. For a single-chain game, call `superroot_atTimestamp` on the configured `--rollup-rpc` op-node; when `--supernode-rpcs` is supplied, use it for shared or interop games requiring a multi-chain op-supernode. Add tests that verify the selected RPC method and reject incompatible source configurations.

topPRs.title: docs: add cross-repo link policy page and CI link-policy linter
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
_Requested by **Matthew Cruz** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1784185257434409)_

Tracks ethereum-optimism/solutions#962 · Plan: [option-b-truth-from-source.md, slice B2](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/solutions/blob/main/projects/docs-improver/plans/option-b-truth-from-source.md) · Program docs: [projects/docs-improver/README.md](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/solutions/tree/main/projects/docs-improver)

## What / why

The docs↔specs↔source link graph rots silently: retired spec paths keep "working" only through a hand-maintained redirect table in the specs repo's `book.toml`, UTM decoration pasted after an anchor breaks the fragment without breaking the page, and commit-pinned contract links never 404 while teaching a two-generations-old architecture. This PR ships the policy that names the canonical form for every cross-repo link, and the deterministic CI linter that enforces it.

### Before

* No written link policy; link form re-litigated (or unnoticed) per PR.
* On `develop` today the linter finds **368 violations**: 291 unbadged sha-/tag-pinned source links (47 pages), 51 retired `/experimental/`-era spec paths, 12 GitHub-blob links into specs sources, 7 query-after-fragment anchors, 3 dead internal links, 2 malformed link targets, 2 unresolved spec anchors.
* No CI gate: any docs PR can add more of each class.

### After

* **Policy page** `op-stack/contribute/link-policy.mdx` (`/op-stack/contribute/link-policy`): rendered specs.optimism.io on current paths; UTM before the `#fragment`; GitHub-blob spec links banned where a rendered page exists; sha-/tag-pins only with an ``as of `` `` badge; deep spec anchors must resolve; root-relative internal links. Written as an annex of the content guide (optimism#21841).
* **Linter** `docs/public-docs/scripts/lint-link-policy.mjs`: dependency-free Node script; vendors the specs `book.toml` redirect table for retired-path detection; resolves spec paths and anchors against a checkout of `ethereum-optimism/specs` using mdBook slug rules; detects dead internal links honoring `docs.json` redirects.
* **Baseline** `scripts/lint-link-policy.baseline.json`: all current findings recorded so **CI blocks only NEW violations** and is green at introduction. The baseline is the burn-down worklist for the follow-up remediation sweep.
* **Fixtures** `docs/lint-link-policy-fixtures/`: one failing fixture per violation class + passing fixtures + a hermetic specs stand-in, run via `--self-test` in CI. Kept outside the Mintlify content root so the deliberate violations never appear in `mint broken-links` output.
* **CI** `.github/workflows/docs-link-policy.yml` (new file, path-filtered to the docs tree): self-test → specs clone → baselined lint; plus `mint broken-links` as an **advisory** job (`continue-on-error`) until the sweep clears the 5 pre-existing broken links recorded on ethereum-optimism/solutions#954 — flip it to blocking then.
* One-line fix: `node-operators/guides/configuration/consensus-clients.mdx` now points at the in-site kona book (`/rust/kona/intro/overview`) instead of the retired external kona book site.

## Verification

* `node scripts/lint-link-policy.mjs --self-test`: all 8 violation classes fire on their failing fixture; passing fixtures are clean.
* Full-tree run against `develop` with specs resolution: 368 findings, all baselined; run exits 0. A canary file with a retired spec path + dead internal link makes the baselined run exit 1 (verified, then removed).
* All 5 pre-existing `mint broken-links` findings from ethereum-optimism/solutions#954 are accounted for: 3 caught as `dead-internal-link`, 1 as `malformed-link`; the 5th (`/operators/chain-operators`) resolves via an explicit `docs.json` redirect, so the linter treats it as alive by design (the sweep should still re-point it).
* `mint broken-links` run locally after moving the fixtures out of the content root: reports only the 5 pre-existing links plus this page's forward-link to the content guide.
* **Specs anchor resolution note:** outbound access to specs.optimism.io is blocked from this session, so spec paths/anchors were resolved against the `ethereum-optimism/specs` repo source (mirrored via raw.githubusercontent.com) — the same thing the CI job does with a real `git clone`. The vendored retired-path table matches the current `book.toml` redirect table.

## docs.json lane

This PR adds a `Contribute` group at the end of the OP Stack tab containing only the policy page. **Synced with develop after #21841 merged; the policy page now sits in the merged Contribute group** (after `content-guide`). The baseline entry that covered this page's forward-link to `/op-stack/contribute/content-guide` was pruned in the sync — the target now exists in-tree — and the self-test + baselined run were re-verified green.

## Out of scope (held, per plan sequencing)

* The **~90-page mechanical remediation sweep** (retired-path rewrites, anchor+UTM fixes, blob→rendered canonicalization, pin badging) — gated on this linter merging so the sweep runs against a merged, trusted check; the committed baseline is its worklist, to be burned down in serialized batches.
* The **bridging-explainer re-point** (`op-stack/bridging/deposit-flow.mdx`, `withdrawal-flow.mdx` off 2023 v1.1.4 links) — optimism#21593 (deposit-flow split) is still in review and touches the same files; runs after it resolves, with an accuracy pass against current `OptimismPortal2`-era contracts.

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] Policy rules match how we actually want links written (especially the ``as of `` `` badge convention for deliberate pins)
- [ ] `docs.json` hunk is the agreed Contribute-group position (now merged into #21841's group)
- [ ] Baseline-gating is acceptable: pre-existing violations pass, new ones block
- [ ] Advisory (non-blocking) status for `mint broken-links` is acceptable until the sweep lands
- [ ] Workflow file: path filters, pinned actions, permissions

topPRs.title: fix(op-revm): discard journal after non-deposit tx errors (SDM warm-set leak)
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
## Summary

`OpHandler::catch_error` reset the EVM journal only on the **deposit** error path. For a **non-deposit** transaction that fails validation (e.g. `NonceTooLow`, or EIP-3607 contract-sender), it returned without calling `journal.discard_tx()`, so the failed tx's partial state — including its **EIP-2929 warm/cold access stamps** — persisted in the shared journal and leaked into the next transaction executed on the same EVM.

On the **SDM `Produce`** execution path (which routes through `inspect_tx`, skipping `finalize()` on error), this means a builder can bill a later included tx a **warm** account access for a tx that never entered the block. A validator re-executing the canonical block (commit-only, `Verify` mode) never ran the skipped tx, recomputes the access as **cold**, and gets a different gas result → **builder-vs-validator divergence → block rejection**.

## Fix

Add the missing `else` branch in `OpHandler::catch_error` calling `journal.discard_tx()` on non-deposit errors, matching upstream revm's `EthHandler::catch_error`. One line of behavior; `rust/op-revm/src/handler.rs`.

This mirrors the same fix independently made upstream in [bluealloy/revm#3780](https://github.com/bluealloy/revm/pull/3780) and in Base's EVM fork ([base/base#3806](https://github.com/base/base/pull/3806)). Note that pulling in revm #3780 alone does **not** fix this on the OP path, because `op-revm` overrides `catch_error`.

## Exposure

Not exploitable on chains running today: with SDM disabled (the current production config) execution uses the `transact` path, whose `finalize()` runs even on error and wipes the failed tx's journal. The leak surfaces only once SDM (`Produce` mode) is active.

## Regression coverage

Two layers, both trigger variants (`NonceTooLow` and EIP-3607), each verified **red without the fix** (2500-gas divergence) and **green with it**:

- **`rust/alloy-op-evm/src/block/tests.rs`** — builder(`Produce`)-vs-validator(`Verify`) block-executor divergence, plus an SDM-disabled safety guard.
- **`rust/op-rbuilder/.../builders/context.rs`** — the sequencer builder's `execute_best_transactions` selection loop: a skipped failed candidate must not warm a later included tx.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p alloy-op-evm --lib block::tests::sdm::warmleak`
- [x] `cargo test -p op-rbuilder --lib builders::context::tests::skipped`
- [x] Each new test confirmed red against the unfixed handler, green against the fix.
